rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's nineteen builder trees go (a row of eucalyptus, ficus, magnolias and jacarandas along the back fences, three queen palms and a norfolk pine 3 m from the house fronts); five come back on their own spots, about one for every two or three houses: by the swing set, on the open south lot corners, and two on the north back fence line 30 m apart.

trees.why: the back yard with the swing set (2.6 m off): shade over the swings
the open lot corner at the south-west, 24 m from the walls: a full jacaranda
the south back lot line, 10 m from the houses: a young eucalyptus between two yards
the north back fence line, 7 m from the house: one of two trees kept from the old row (one every 6 m)
the same line's east end, 30 m on, 7 m from the house
